verses.text: The famine was still terrible in the land.
When they had eaten all the grain they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, "Go back and buy us a little more food."
But Judah said to him, "The man strongly warned us, 'You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.'
If you will send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you.
But if you will not send him, we will not go down, because the man said to us, 'You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.'"
Israel asked, "Why did you bring this trouble on me by telling the man you had another brother?"

They replied, "The man questioned us closely about ourselves and our family. He asked us, 'Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother?' We simply answered his questions. How could we possibly know he would say, 'Bring your brother down here'?"
Then Judah said to his father Israel, "Send the boy with me, and we will go at once, so that we and you and our children can live and not die.

I myself promise to keep him safe. You can hold me personally responsible for him. If I do not bring him back to you and set him here in front of you, I will bear the blame in front of you for the rest of my life.
If we had not wasted so much time, we could have gone and come back twice by now."

Then their father Israel said to them, "If it must be, then do this. Put some of the best things from our land in your bags and take them down to the man as a gift: a little healing balm and a little honey, some spices and myrrh, some pistachio nuts and almonds.
Take twice the amount of silver with you, because you must give back the silver that was put back in the tops of your sacks. Perhaps it was a mistake.
Take your brother too, and go back to the man at once.
And may God Almighty make the man kind to you, so that he will let your other brother and Benjamin come back with you. As for me, if I lose my children, then I lose them."
So the men took the gifts and twice the amount of silver, and Benjamin too. They hurried down to Egypt and stood in front of Joseph.
When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the man in charge of his house, "Take these men to my house. Kill an animal and prepare a meal, because they are going to eat with me at noon."
The man did as Joseph told him and took the men to Joseph's house.

Now the men were frightened when they were taken to his house. They thought, "We were brought here because of the silver that was put back in our sacks the first time. He wants to attack us and overpower us, and take us as slaves and take our donkeys."
So they went up to the man in charge of Joseph's house and spoke to him at the entrance to the house.
"Please, sir," they said, "we came down here the first time to buy food.
But at the place where we stopped for the night, we opened our sacks, and each of us found his silver, the exact amount, in the top of his sack. So we have brought it back with us.
We have also brought more silver with us to buy food. We do not know who put our silver in our sacks."
"It is all right," he said. "Do not be afraid. Your God, the God of your father, must have put treasure in your sacks for you. I received your silver." Then he brought Simeon out to them.
The man took the men into Joseph's house. He gave them water to wash their feet and food for their donkeys.
They got their gifts ready for Joseph's arrival at noon, because they had heard that they were going to eat there.
When Joseph came home, they brought him the gifts they had carried into the house, and they bowed down to the ground in front of him.
He asked them how they were, and then he said, "How is your old father you told me about? Is he still alive?"
They replied, "Your servant our father is still alive and well." And they bowed down low to show him honour.
As Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, his own mother's son, he asked, "Is this your youngest brother, the one you told me about?" And he said, "May God be kind to you, my son."
Joseph was so deeply moved at the sight of his brother that he hurried out, looking for a place to weep. He went into his private room and wept there.
After he had washed his face, he came out. Controlling himself, he said, "Serve the food."
They served him by himself, the brothers by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves. Egyptians would not eat with Hebrews, because they thought that was disgraceful.
The brothers had been seated in front of him in the order of their ages, from the firstborn to the youngest, and they looked at each other in amazement.
Portions of food were taken to them from Joseph's table, but Benjamin's portion was five times as much as anyone else's. So they feasted and drank freely with him.
